p114.002: This paper tells us how unseen heavenly beings are looking after our world. The Urantia Book says that “⟦Q 114:6.8⟧the Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men⟦/Q⟧”, and this work is done mainly through the seraphim, that is, the angels. According to the archangel who wrote this paper, at noon on one day there were more than five hundred million pairs of angels on our world.
p114.003: The heavenly government of our world is unlike that of any other world in the universe. That is because it was a world where life was planted with some experimental changes, it went through confusion from the Lucifer rebellion and the failure of Adam, and it is the world where Michael, the Creator Son of our universe, was born as a human being. So our world came to need a special kind of supervision.
p114.005: After Caligastia, the Planetary Prince who ruled our world, betrayed God in the Lucifer rebellion, our world was for a long time not properly connected with the universe government. Only after Michael finished his life on earth as Jesus was he proclaimed the Planetary Prince of our world. But Michael does not rule directly; he has entrusted the work to a commission of twenty-four who once lived on our world.
p114.006: Recently Machiventa Melchizedek, who came to this world in human form long ago in the days of Abraham, was named Planetary Prince to act for Michael. Opinions differ on when he will actually come, but the writer expects that he could appear on any day, at any time.
p114.008: The commission of twenty-four planetary supervisors is located on Jerusem, the capital of our system. All of them were true leaders when they lived on this world, and they received further training on the mansion worlds. When this commission meets, its chairman is said to be the man we know as ‘John the Baptist.’
p114.009: They advise not only our world but also thirty-six other worlds isolated by the rebellion, yet they take a special interest in the welfare and progress of the people of our world. No one knows how long they will hold this task.
p114.011: Every hundred years the commission sends one of its members to our world to stay as resident governor general. While this paper was being prepared, the nineteenth governor general was replaced by the twentieth. The governor general’s name is not given, because people tend to look up to outstanding beings too easily and treat them like gods.
p114.012: The governor general is less a ruler with great authority of his own than a fatherly adviser. Even so, he makes dozens of decisions every day, and all the angels working on our world and the midwayers, the unseen beings between humans and angels, follow him as their leader.
p114.014: An observer who represents the Most Highs of Edentia also stays on our world. He is a high being called a Vorondadek Son, and since the rebellion he has held certain powers over our world. When a great crisis comes, this observer can become regent and directly lead the government of our world, and this has happened thirty-three times in the history of our world.
p114.015: This observer also advises the race commissioners, the beings who watch over the condition of the various races. And the Most Highs do not step in only on worlds where there was rebellion; whenever needed, they can add the greater wisdom of the constellation rulers to the affairs of any world. The Urantia Book explains, however, that purely spiritual matters seem to be handled by the commander of the archangels, who has headquarters on our world.
p114.017: The heavenly government of our world does not have clearly separate legislative, executive, and judicial branches as our countries do. The commission of twenty-four is close to a legislature, the governor general serves as an advising representative, and disputes are settled by the courts of conciliation. The empty place left by the missing Planetary Prince is filled jointly by the archangels, the Most High observer, and the governor general.
p114.018: Our world is formally isolated in spirit, but in an emergency it can use the archangels’ circuit of communication. Besides that, because the Spirit of Truth was poured out on all people about nineteen hundred years ago, this isolation hardly matters for each individual person. The day’s administration of our world is said to begin with a council where the governor general, the chief of archangels, the Most High observer, the chief of the Life Carriers, and others meet together to talk things over. It may look like a loose organization, but it works much better than you might expect.
p114.019: 6. The Master Seraphim of Planetary Supervision
p114.020: When the Spirit of Truth was poured out, twelve groups of special angels came to our world. These are the master seraphim of planetary supervision. There are the angels who lead the ages, the angels of progress who lead advancement, the religious guardians who protect good values, and the angels who help the political life of nations. There are also the angels of the races, the angels who prepare for the future, the angels of enlightenment who help education, the angels of health, the angels who guard the home, the angels of industry, the angels of diversion who help with play, humor, and rest, and the angels who look after other heavenly beings.
p114.021: Interestingly, the angels of progress try to make the world new, while the religious guardians try to keep the good values of the old, so the two balance each other. These angels do not force anything on people. They cannot push new ideas into the human mind, but they strengthen the high ideals that have already risen within a person. They bring good ideas together and little by little guide circumstances so that plans can be carried out. When angels disagree among themselves, the governor general usually settles the matter.
p114.023: The angels also prepare a group of living people called the reserve corps of destiny. These are big-hearted, moral, and spiritually deep people who are quietly trained so that they can be used to keep civilization from collapsing or the light of truth from going out when a great crisis comes to the world. When this paper was written, there were 962 of them on our world in twelve corps, and most of them do not know that they are such people. They are people who are glad to serve without human recognition or reward. They are quietly trained deep in their minds with the help of their Thought Adjusters and guardian angels, and they also help important knowledge pass from one generation to the next. They hardly appear in history books, but they are the people who have held their places when civilization was in danger.
p114.024: The Urantia Book says again and again that our world is not an orphan abandoned in the universe. The whole universe, all the way to Paradise, knows that we are here, and we are cared for even more lovingly than worlds that never had a rebellion. The Urantia Book closes this paper with the words “⟦Q 114:7.17⟧the Father himself loves you⟦/Q⟧”. Even when the world looks troubled, it is a great comfort to know that many unseen hands are caring for us.
p115.002: Starting with this paper, we talk about the Supreme Being, the God who grows along with the universe. Between God the Father and us, the most important thing is the fact that we are his children. But in our relationship with God the Supreme, what matters is actually achieving something. The Urantia Book says that “⟦Q 115:0.1⟧one must do something as well as be something⟦/Q⟧”.
p115.004: The human mind cannot know the true beginning and end of everything. So in order to think, it first sets up a frame of thought of its own and then reasons step by step inside it. Such frames are necessary, but they always have some parts that are not quite right. The Urantia Book compares these frames to useful scaffolding that must be taken down as our understanding grows.
p115.005: Our understanding of truth, beauty, love, and even God is all relative truth. God is much greater than a Father, but the idea of the Father is the highest concept of God that human beings have. In higher worlds ahead we will gain wider ideas about God. And The Urantia Book says that the finite world, the limited world we live in, exists because God willed it so.
p115.007: Everything is already contained in the infinity of God. Yet seen through the eyes of limited creatures, there are countless possibilities that have not yet come true. The Urantia Book explains that the whole plan of universe creation and evolution is a process of turning ‘potential’ into ‘actual.’ On our world, this happens through evolution and experience.
p115.008: The Urantia Book says we cannot know how the value of what is infinite and divine could grow any greater. But in the experiencing universe, the more deeply we understand the meaning of reality, the more real divine values become. This change happens together in every realm: space, mind, and spirit.
p115.010: The Infinite One cannot be fully expressed in any words. To understand the infinite, the human mind has no choice but to divide it into parts and think about them one by one. The Urantia Book explains it by dividing it into the Father, who is the source of all things, the things that already actually exist, and the possibilities of what can still come to be. The tension among these three is what makes growth happen in the universe. The Urantia Book says that the human spirit can reach the infinite Father in worship, but the greatest concept the human intellect can grasp goes only as far as the Supreme Being. It also says that even if some things are not fulfilled in part, taken as a whole the will of God is in the end surely done.
p115.011: The Urantia Book says there is never an end to growth in the universe. Whenever one thing is achieved, a new path of possibility always opens. Each decision we make not only creates a new experience but also opens up a new capacity to grow. The Urantia Book says that “⟦Q 115:3.16⟧The man lives in every child⟦/Q⟧”. What looks like an end from a small point of view is, from a large point of view, just the passage to the next stage.
p115.013: The Supreme Being came from the Paradise Trinity, the Deity in which the Father, the Son, and the Spirit are one. The spirit personality of the Supreme Being came from the Trinity, and the power by which he grows comes from the relation between the actuals and the potentials of the universe.
p115.014: How can the infinite God reach us who are limited? The Urantia Book says that the Thought Adjuster living within us is the proof. The absolute God meets directly even with the smallest and weakest creature.
p115.015: 5. Relation of the Supreme to the Paradise Trinity
p115.016: The Supreme Being depends completely on the Trinity for his personality and spirit nature. The Trinity always remains a perfect and unshakable center, and the Supreme Being grows little by little around it. As time goes on, the creating once done directly by the Trinity gradually passes over to the creating done by the children of God.
p115.017: 6. Relation of the Supreme to the Triodities
p115.018: The Supreme Being moves in two directions. One is the movement reaching out from Paradise into the outer universe, like the Creator Sons. The other is the movement of gathering in from the outer universe toward Paradise, like ascenders such as us. Just as we recognize the unseen wind by the trembling of the leaves, heavenly beings are said to sense the movement of the Supreme Being by watching the changes taking place in the universe. The farther from Paradise, the more the universe depends on possibilities not yet realized, and the Supreme Being grows by turning those possibilities into reality.
p115.020: Because God the Supreme is a God who grows by experiencing, he goes through the limits of time and the process of growth. The Urantia Book explains that this is the Father’s plan. That plan bases progress on effort, achievement on perseverance, and the growth of personality on faith. That is why we, though limited, can live in the universe and someday reach the divinity of the Supreme Being.
p115.021: The Urantia Book describes God the Supreme as ‘the finite shadow’ cast across the universe by the infinite Father. The fact that every step of our growing, as we try, endure, and believe, is added to the growth of God the Supreme means that even our small efforts have meaning for the whole universe.
p116.002: When you look at the world, you sometimes wonder why there is so much unfairness and confusion. The Urantia Book explains that Havona, the perfect central universe, was made by the perfect Creator, but our world has been made and is being cared for by creators who are not yet perfect. Once we know this, The Urantia Book says, religion will no longer offer only resignation to the poor and only self-satisfaction to the well-off in the face of unfairness.
p116.003: Havona was perfect from the beginning and does not grow. But the grand universe we belong to is a growing universe. The Almighty Supreme is a living God in whom power and personality grow together. His destiny is perfection, but for now he is still growing. According to The Urantia Book, the Supreme Being works as a spirit personality in the central universe and, in the grand universe, as God the Almighty, a personality of power. No one knows exactly what third role he will take on in the outer universes in the future.
p116.005: The experience of every evolving creature in the universe is a part of the experience of the Almighty Supreme. What ties power and personality together into one in the Supreme Being is the Supreme Mind. The Urantia Book honestly admits that the Supreme Mind is what we know least about.
p116.006: Still, one thing is certain. The body stops growing once it is fully grown, and spirit can reach perfection, but mind never stops growing. Mind is the way of experience that goes on without end. This is why we can keep learning all our lives, and forever.
p116.007: 2. The Almighty and God the Sevenfold
p116.008: We who live in time and space cannot fully understand the infinite God of Paradise. So God reveals himself in several levels so that we can come near him. This is called God the Sevenfold. In the order in which we meet them, they are the Creator Son and Creative Spirit who made our universe, the Ancients of Days of the superuniverse, the Seven Master Spirits, the Supreme Being, the Infinite Spirit, the Eternal Son, and the Universal Father.
p116.009: The first three levels are the creators who make and govern the universes, and the last three are the Deities of Paradise. In between them is the Supreme Being. The Supreme Being receives his personality from the Trinity and grows by gaining power through the activities of the creators. That does not mean that the Supreme Being simply is the Trinity, or the creators added together. He is a newly appearing God who is connected with all of them, and in the present universe age he is the greatest revelation of God.
p116.011: The Deities of Paradise also take part directly in the evolution of the universe. The Infinite Spirit gives mind to every creature and links matter with spirit. The Eternal Son and his Sons actually live the life of creatures. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 116:3.3⟧When divinity becomes like humanity, inherent in this relationship is the possibility that humanity can become divine⟦/Q⟧”.
p116.012: The Universal Father lives within us as the Thought Adjuster. Just as the Trinity is the unshakable foundation of the Supreme Being, the Adjuster is our unshakable foundation. On that foundation, our free choices go on making our eternal selves.
p116.013: 4. The Almighty and the Supreme Creators
p116.014: The growth of the Supreme Being depends on the many parts of the universe coming together into one. The Seven Master Spirits and the Ancients of Days are important beings who help this growth. But The Urantia Book says that the local universe is the real laboratory where mind and personality grow.
p116.015: In the local universe even the creators grow. A Creator Son lives the life of a creature several times and so comes to know the hearts of his children. Sons who came to this world, like Jesus, did not make a new road to God; they lit up brightly the eternal road that was already there. The Urantia Book says that even people like us are necessary for God the Sevenfold to work fully.
p116.016: 5. The Almighty and the Sevenfold Controllers
p116.017: God the Sevenfold includes not only the creators who make the universes but also the controllers who direct the physical energies of the universe. The Almighty Supreme is growing into the one who directs the physical powers of the grand universe.
p116.018: The universes of time are not yet perfect, and their destiny is to strive toward perfection. This striving happens not only in mind and spirit but also in energy and matter. Because new energy and matter keep appearing as the universe goes on growing, the universe cannot reach complete stability until it is settled in light and life. In the end all energy responds to mind, and the controllers who direct energy work without ceasing to keep matter in balance. The Urantia Book suggests that on the day the universe reaches complete material balance, the physical control of the Almighty will be complete.
p116.020: In the universe where we live, the power of matter is strong, but within a personality, spirit tries to rule matter through mind. On Paradise, energy and spirit are one, but in a faraway local universe the gap between them is very wide, so mind has to link the two.
p116.021: A wide gap means the problem is hard, but it also means there is the chance for greater experience. The human body can follow the mind, and the mind can be led by spirit. The Urantia Book says that everyone, from human beings to the Supreme Being, “⟦Q 116:6.8⟧All strive, personally strive, in the achievement⟦/Q⟧”.
p116.022: 7. The Living Organism of the Grand Universe
p116.023: The grand universe is not a huge lump of matter; it is like a vast living being that breathes. Just as our bodies have nerves and blood vessels, the universe has circuits of intelligence and channels of energy stretching through it. Just as we live by depending on sunlight, the universe moves by depending on the energy that comes from Paradise.
p116.024: When we seek God and strive to become perfect, a holy tension arises in the universe. This tension is resolved as our souls grow. And the great tension that arises when all creatures and creators seek God together is resolved into oneness in the Supreme Being. It is a wonderful encouragement to know that my small effort to draw near to God is connected with the growth of the whole universe.
p117.002: Wherever we are, every time we do the will of God, God the Supreme becomes one step more real. If every being in the grand universe came to live by the will of God, the whole universe would reach light and life, a state of complete peace and maturity, and then God the Supreme would fully appear. The growth of each part of the universe reflects the growth of the Supreme Being, and the Supreme Being is all that growth added together.
p117.004: The Supreme Being is the beauty of physical harmony, the truth of thought, and the goodness of spiritual values. The Urantia Book calls him “⟦Q 117:1.1⟧the sweetness of true success and the joy of everlasting achievement⟦/Q⟧”. He is the great soul of the grand universe, the one in whom the experience shared by creators and creatures has become a personality.
p117.005: In the universe there is a long procession of creators who come down from Paradise to show us God, and of creatures who climb up from below seeking God. These two come to understand each other and become eternal brothers. Just as Michael showed the love of the Father, those who received that love want to share love with their brothers and sisters too. Love like this is exactly what reflects the love of God the Supreme.
p117.007: The Supreme Being is God in time, and the secret of our growing in time lies in him. For a human being, to live means to grow. The Urantia Book explains that in the present universe age, creatures can grow because the Supreme Being is still growing. Certain beings who already have a finished status no longer grow in this way.
p117.008: So The Urantia Book says that the fact that the Supreme Being is not yet complete is actually a good thing, because an empty cup can be filled. The reason we can dream of Paradise is also that we are in the Supreme Being and are sharing in his growth.
p117.009: 3. Significance of the Supreme to Universe Creatures
p117.010: Jesus said, “⟦Q 117:3.3⟧I am the living way⟦/Q⟧”. Just as Jesus is the living way from the human level to God, the Supreme Being is also the living way by which we, though limited, move on to a higher consciousness. The Urantia Book says that human beings are made in the image of God in more than a figure of speech. That is because the way the Adjuster and our will together grow an immortal soul within us resembles the way the Supreme Being grows in the universe.
p117.011: Just as the Trinity is the unshakable foundation for God the Supreme, the Adjuster is that kind of foundation for us. The Urantia Book says that “⟦Q 117:3.12⟧we actually live, move, and have our being within the immanence of the Supreme⟦/Q⟧”. The Supreme Being did not create us directly, but our life came out of his potential.
p117.013: The way every being in the universe strives to become perfect reflects the effort of God the Supreme to complete himself. When a person chooses eternal life, the Supreme Being grows that much. But if a person refuses to the very end, the person’s good values remain, yet the person himself disappears like a drop of water returning to the sea, and the growth of the Supreme Being is delayed by that much.
p117.014: Because of this, the choice of each person carries a cosmic responsibility. The Urantia Book says that personality has a value no one else can take the place of. My part is a contribution of my own that no one else can fill for me. The Urantia Book tells us a mysterious fact. The closer a person comes to God in love, the more real that person becomes, and the more a person gives his will to the Father, the greater God makes him than he was before.
p117.016: The Supreme Being is the oversoul of creation, the great soul of the whole universe. Following the will of God does not make our personality disappear. Rather, the more we take part in this great adventure, the richer we become. The Urantia Book passes on the saying “⟦Q 117:5.5⟧The act is ours, the consequences God's⟦/Q⟧”.
p117.017: The help of mind and spirit we received on this world does not become our possession; it remains part of the Supreme Being. What we carry with us forever instead is character. The Urantia Book says that true character is the sum of decisions that are lit up by sincere worship, made bright by wise love, and completed in service to our brothers and sisters. Even after we leave our universe, the Spirit of Truth keeps guiding us, always whispering, “⟦Q 117:5.9⟧This is the way.⟦/Q⟧”
p117.019: The Urantia Book says that if God is our Father, the Supreme Being is like a mother who raises us in the universe. That is why finding him is like coming home. The Urantia Book says that God is the greatest experience a human being can have, and that to find God is to find everything.
p117.020: All true love comes from God. Love cannot be locked up in the heart; it becomes ours only when we share it with our neighbors. The Father’s love comes to us through the Adjuster, flows through us to our brothers and sisters, and in that way reaches the Supreme Being. The Urantia Book says that we can find the Father in our own hearts, but we must find the Supreme Being in the hearts of all other people.
p117.021: We do not discover the Supreme Being suddenly, the way an earthquake splits a rock. We discover him slowly and patiently, the way a river quietly wears away the land. A person who knows God is never lonely while traveling through the universe, because the Father walks beside him, and the very road he walks on is the presence of the Supreme Being.
p117.023: Someday, when all the possibilities have come true, the Supreme Being will fully appear as the almighty God of the grand universe. Ascenders who reach Paradise will pledge eternal loyalty to God the Supreme, and the disharmony and discord of the universe will at last disappear.
p117.024: When that time comes, the thrilling adventure of making harmony out of chaos and beauty out of possibility may end, and the universe may rest for a while. But before long, a greater mystery called God the Ultimate will bring new challenges. Our seeking God and growing here on earth right now is the very first step of this endless adventure.
p118.002: If God the Supreme is the God who grows along with the grand universe we live in, God the Ultimate is the God beyond time and space who is connected with the whole master universe, which is even wider. Just as God the Sevenfold is necessary for the growth of God the Supreme, God the Supreme is necessary for God the Ultimate to appear. These two are bridges that link the growth of the universe from beginning to end.
p118.003: The Urantia Book uses numbers as an example. No matter how large a number you think of, you can always add one more. Growth is endless like that, but along the way there are joyful moments of reaching goals. After tasting that joy, we soon begin to dream of an even greater goal, and this adventure goes on forever.
p118.005: When a person makes up his mind to do the Father’s will, that decision becomes something eternal that does not change no matter how much time passes. It makes no difference whether a million moments go by or a billion. In this way the choice of a human being and the choice of God meet, and an eternal union comes into being.
p118.006: The more mature a person becomes, the more he judges the present by thinking about both past experience and future plans together. The Urantia Book says that if patience is what a person who sees time in short spans needs, true maturity goes beyond patience with a tolerance born of deep understanding. To mature is to live the present more fully without being bound only to the present.
p118.008: With the help of God the Sevenfold, we come to know God little by little. In Havona we discover God the Supreme, on Paradise we meet him as a person, and after that we try to know God the Ultimate. The Urantia Book says that at whatever stage we discover God, in the end we are meeting the same Paradise Father, who appears in wider and wider ways.
p118.010: Of all the animals, only human beings can understand time and space together. Things are bound by time, but truth goes beyond time. The Urantia Book says that the more truth we know and the more truthful we become, the better we can understand the past and the better we can look ahead into the future. Truth is not shaken by any shock, and yet it is always alive and shining.
p118.012: The Urantia Book says that much theological confusion comes from attributing everything directly to the infinite God. The true first cause is God, but beneath him there are countless secondary causes that come from God. The Creator Sons are not creators who make things new out of nothing; they turn possibilities that have already been prepared into reality. Still, from our point of view, they truly do create.
p118.014: God being all-powerful does not mean that he does impossible things. Even God cannot make a square circle or a good evil. God does not do what is ungodlike.
p118.015: At first the Father does everything, but as time goes on it becomes clear that creatures, even human beings, must become God’s partners. When human beings and God become partners, there is no limit to what is possible. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 118:5.3⟧Always must God first find man that man may later find God⟦/Q⟧”.
p118.017: God is all-powerful, but he does not do everything himself. If we think that God personally does everything, we ignore the countless Creator Sons and workers, and our own free will as well. The Urantia Book calls this idea the great error of pantheism.
p118.018: Human choice has limits. A person cannot choose to be something other than a human being, but he can choose to be more than a human being. The Urantia Book says that the choice to seek God and to become like God is the one choice that goes beyond finite limits.
p118.020: An experienced adult can often guess ahead of time what a little brother or sister will choose, but that does not make the child’s choice any less free. God’s knowing ahead of time does not make our choices fake either. God has simply set wise limits on the range within which a still-young will can move.
p118.021: If there is real freedom, there must also be the possibility of choosing wrongly. The Urantia Book explains sin as the immaturity of being so excited by freedom that one fails to see one’s responsibilities as a citizen of the universe. That is why, at the lower stages, the range of choice is narrowly limited to protect us, and the more we become like the will of God, the freer our choices become.
p118.023: In some ways a human being is like a living machine. But he is more than a machine, for he has a mind and a spirit dwells with him. In primitive times people had little power to control themselves, so outward limits such as time and space, hunger and fear protected them. Slow progress also acts as a brake that guards against the dangers that too-rapid change would bring. When material progress runs too far ahead of wisdom, civilization slips backward.
p118.024: The Urantia Book says that the mistake of Caligastia and Lucifer was exactly that they tried to force off this brake of time. Each time we overcome one outward limit, we must fill its place with a limit we choose ourselves. That is justice and brotherhood. The Urantia Book says that the greatest adventure of a human being is to grow spiritually, declaring in each moment of life, “⟦Q 118:8.11⟧It is my will that your will be done.⟦/Q⟧”
p118.026: Time and space are arrangements that let us, though limited, live in the presence of the Infinite One. Without them we could not exist, but because of them our actions are limited. Within those limits our will is relatively free. The Urantia Book says that the grand universe is both a living organism and a precise mechanism at the same time, and explains that the order of the universe is like the crystallized thought of the Creator.
p118.028: Providence does not mean that God has decided everything about us ahead of time. God loves us too much to do that. The Urantia Book says that God’s love is not a blind love that spoils his children. Providence works for the good of the whole, and whenever there is need, the Father can lovingly step into events.
p118.029: What we call good luck may actually be bad luck, and hard trouble may actually be the tempering fire that turns soft iron into hard steel. When we pray for providence, in many cases the answer is a change in our own attitude toward life. The Urantia Book says that the kingdom of God is in the hearts of men. The faith that both good things and hard things work together for the growth of a person who seeks God gives us the strength to live today without being shaken.
p119.002: This paper is the story, told by Gavalia, the chief of the Evening Stars, of how Michael, the Creator of our universe, gave himself seven times. This is called a ‘bestowal.’ A Creator Son is actually born in the form of the creatures he made and lives just as they do, and he must finish this successfully seven times before he can become the full ruler of his own universe.
p119.003: Creator Sons are just and merciful by nature. But by actually living the life of a creature, they gain a new kind of understanding mercy, fair judgment, and patience. Above all, a bestowal is the final training for the Creator himself to become a wise and warm-hearted ruler. Michael began making our universe of Nebadon about four hundred billion years ago, and his bestowals followed one another about every one hundred fifty million years, with the last one taking place on our world nineteen hundred years ago.
p119.005: Almost a billion years ago, Michael left the universe in the care of his elder brother Immanuel, and with the words “⟦Q 119:1.2⟧I leave you but for a short season⟦/Q⟧”, he disappeared before everyone’s eyes. Three days later, on the world of the Melchizedeks, a stranger Melchizedek appeared who looked exactly like them. The Melchizedeks are the wise teachers of our universe and the Sons who help in emergencies.
p119.006: For a hundred years this stranger Melchizedek faithfully served on twenty-four emergency missions, won everyone’s respect with his outstanding wisdom and love, and became the chief of the Melchizedeks. Then one day at noon he disappeared as quietly as he had come. Everyone believes he was Michael. No one knows how a Creator can become a being he himself made, but it really happened.
p119.008: At the time of the second bestowal, Lutentia, the ruler of a system, started a rebellion. After he was removed, Michael appeared in that troubled system in the form of a Lanonandek Son, a Son who governs systems, and became its temporary ruler. He restored order with justice and mercy, and he even offered the rebel Lutentia a share in the rule if only he would repent.
p119.009: Lutentia refused to the end, but millions who had been misled accepted forgiveness. On the day the new ruler arrived and Michael left, everyone mourned parting with the most noble and gentle ruler they had ever known. Even the rebel sent a message: “⟦Q 119:2.6⟧Just and righteous are you in all your ways⟦/Q⟧”.
p119.011: The third time, Michael appeared in the form of a Material Son, the same order as Adam, on a planet swept up in rebellion. On that world, cut off from contact with the outer universe, he worked alone for a generation, led the fallen Planetary Prince and his staff to repent, and brought that world back to God’s side.
p119.012: The Urantia Book says this story is one of the most beautiful and touching scenes in the history of our universe. Since then, no Material Son or Daughter has ever complained that their task is too hard, because they know that the Creator who was tested in every way just as they are understands them.
p119.014: The fourth time, Michael became one of the seraphim, an angel. For more than forty years he worked on twenty-two worlds as an angel secretary assisting various teachers. During that time the angels did not know which one was Michael, so they gave special respect to every angel. Anyone at all might, without knowing it, be working alongside the Master of the universe.
p119.015: In this way Michael experienced, one after another, three orders of the Sons he had made and then came down to be an angel, and now he turned his eyes to the path walked by mortals, the lowest will creatures, the people who go through death.
p119.017: The fifth time, Michael appeared on Uversa, the headquarters of the superuniverse, in the form of an ascending mortal who had reached the spirit stage. The people there called him Eventod. For eleven years he worked and was tested just like the other ascenders, and he always had the respect of his companions.
p119.018: Watching this, the beings of the universe began to realize that Michael would someday be born in a human body too. The fact that the Creator himself walked the path of an ascender added new meaning to the whole plan of human beings rising to God.
p119.020: The sixth time, Michael lived at the headquarters of a constellation in the form of a morontia mortal, an ascender who is growing on the mansion worlds after death. The Urantia Book says this life was a truly amazing time, but it cannot tell about it in detail.
p119.021: When he returned from this bestowal, it was clear to everyone that the Creator had become a fellow of his creatures and a friend even to the lowest of beings. When countless beings gathered to give thanks, Michael answered, “⟦Q 119:6.5⟧I have simply been about my Father's business.⟦/Q⟧”
p119.023: Soon after Adam and Eve failed, Michael announced that he would make his final bestowal on our world. From then on, our little world drew the attention of the whole universe. Until then Michael had always appeared fully grown, so the news that he had been born as a helpless baby in Bethlehem amazed the whole universe.
p119.024: Joshua ben Joseph, that is, Jesus, was conceived and born like every other baby, and he grew up under ordinary parents like the children of his time. How the Creator became a human being is a mystery that will never be solved. The only supernatural event connected with his birth was that an angel announced it to a priest of Chaldea named Ardnon and his companions.
p119.026: After finishing his final bestowal on our world, Michael was recognized by the Universal Father and the rulers of the superuniverse as the full ruler of Nebadon. He was born a Creator, but his sovereignty he had to earn himself through experience lasting almost a billion years. In his seven bestowals he revealed the will of God in a different way each time, and finally, on our world, he lived out the will of the Universal Father as a human being of flesh and blood.
p119.027: The Urantia Book tells us that our world is a sanctuary that the whole universe of Nebadon holds dear in its heart, and that Michael has promised to come back here someday. The fact that the Creator of the universe came down to the lowest place and lived just as we do in order to understand us tells us that, in any hardship, we are never alone.
p120.002: This paper tells what happened just before Michael was born on our world as Jesus. A Creator Son must live the very same life as the beings he made before he can become the full ruler of his own universe. Michael had already finished six bestowals, and now he prepared to come down to our world in the body of a human being, the lowest will creature.
p120.003: In fact, as the Creator, Michael could have ruled the universe by his own right at any time. But he did not want to do it that way. He hoped to become a wiser ruler by deeply understanding his creatures and through the experience of freely following the will of the Paradise Deities. So in each of his seven bestowals he followed a different will of the Trinity, and in the last one, on our world, he chose to follow the will of the Universal Father completely.
p120.004: In this way Michael’s rule became not a power he used however he liked, but an authority that came out of his experience with the Paradise Deities and his experience of living as a creature. The Urantia Book says that his power is unlimited, his authority is beyond question, and his sovereignty is supreme.
p120.005: Before leaving, Michael entrusted the universe to his elder brother Immanuel. On behalf of the Universal Father, Immanuel gave Michael counsel for his final bestowal. Michael chose this path not because anyone ordered him to but because he himself wanted to, and his decision to place himself once again in the Father’s will meant that he would experience both human nature and the Father’s will together.
p120.007: Immanuel said this: in his earlier bestowals Michael had always appeared fully grown, but this time he would be born as a helpless baby, so it would be a completely new experience. He also said that on our world Michael should lay aside every special help from heaven by his own choice and depend only on the Paradise Father.
p120.008: So there was only one thing Michael needed to take care of: keeping his unbroken communion with the Father. Immanuel would keep the universe safe, and it was arranged that no rebellion could break out while Michael was on our world. When Michael finished this experience, Immanuel said, he would know for himself what the faith and trust he had always hoped for from his creatures really are.
p120.010: Immanuel asked several things of Michael. He advised him to grow up as a child on our world, to learn as a human being, to live by the Father’s will, and, as the Son of Man, to bring the Lucifer rebellion to an end. Since he had not crushed the rebels with the power of a Creator, this time he was to accomplish it in the form of the lowest creature, in the weakness of trusting the Father.
p120.011: Above all, Immanuel told him to become a teacher, first to set people’s spirits free, to light up darkened minds, to heal souls, and to release people from age-old fears. After he left, he was to pour out the Spirit of Truth so that all people could receive Thought Adjusters. His life was not to be a pattern for the people of one age to copy, but a life that would inspire every world and every generation in the universe.
p120.012: The greatest mission was to show God to human beings through a life of doing the Father’s will. At the same time, it was to show the whole universe how high a God-knowing person can grow during a short life. In one single life he would show God seeking man and man seeking and finding God. Immanuel also urged Michael to take care, since he still had the power of a Creator, not to let himself want to do superhuman things apart from the Father’s will.
p120.014: Immanuel added a few more pieces of advice. He told Michael to live by the family customs of his time, not to get tangled up in economic or political problems, and not to interfere with the natural development of humanity. He could take part in the existing religions, but he should keep any new sect or rigid religion from forming. That was because his life and teachings were to become the common heritage of all religions and all peoples.
p120.015: That is why Jesus left no writings and did not allow anyone to paint or carve his likeness. He wanted nothing to be left behind that people could worship like an idol after he was gone. Immanuel also said that, following the rule that a Son from Paradise leaves no descendants on a world, he would not marry. Everything else was left to the leading of the Adjuster and the spirit, and to the judgment of his own mind. After receiving Immanuel’s blessing, Michael quietly disappeared before everyone’s eyes.
p120.017: Some of the rebels had accused Michael of being a ruler who cared only for his own power. But his life as the Son of Man, following the Father’s will, forgetting himself, and serving others, silenced that accusation forever.
p120.018: The Urantia Book says clearly that Jesus was not a being with two personalities. He was not God joined with a man but God in man, and from beginning to end he was both God and man. The only thing that changed as he grew up was that he came to realize this fact more and more for himself. For the beings of the local universe there are hardly any miracles, but they count the Son of God becoming a man through a natural process as the most amazing miracle, one that even they cannot understand. The Urantia Book says that the highest purpose of this bestowal was to reveal God more clearly. The fact that God came among us in the most ordinary and natural way tells us that our ordinary days, too, can become places where we meet God.
p121.002: With this paper, the story of the life of Jesus begins. The writer is a secondary midwayer who was once assigned to help the apostle Andrew. Midwayers are unseen beings, somewhere between humans and angels, who stay and work on our world. He says he will write down the life of Jesus based on what his fellow midwayers saw for themselves and on the records Andrew left behind. Because Jesus did not want to leave written records, the apostles also hesitated for a long time to write the gospels.
p121.003: 1. The Occident of the First Century after Christ
p121.004: Jesus did not come in a spiritually dark age. The Urantia Book says that the world at that time had the best conditions for a Creator Son to come. Greek culture and the Greek language had spread widely, and Rome was ruling the Mediterranean world with tolerance. Europe was bound together under three influences: the political system of Rome, the language and culture of Greece, and the religion and morals of the Jews.
p121.005: Good roads linked the great cities, and pirates had disappeared from the seas, so trade and travel grew greatly. But even though things looked peaceful on the surface, most people lived in poverty, and there was hardly any happy middle class.
p121.007: The Jews lived at a crossroads of world trade. Palestine was the crossroads where three continents met, and more than half of the caravans coming from the East passed near Nazareth, a small village in Galilee. The synagogues of the Jews scattered all over the Roman world later became the places where the new gospel was first received. You could say that Greece provided the language, Rome the roads, and the Jews the synagogues.
p121.008: Even under Rome the Jews governed themselves to some degree, and they expected that the Messiah, a great deliverer, would soon come. They believed they had kept their independence because they were the “⟦Q 121:2.8⟧chosen people⟦/Q⟧”, but they refused to learn that their mission was spiritual, not political. It was the time when Herod the Idumean ruled, so the people were uneasy. At the time Jesus was born, Galilee was more gentile than Jewish.
p121.010: Roman society was divided into five classes: the aristocracy, the merchants, a small middle class, free laborers, and slaves. Half of the population were slaves, but talented slaves sometimes saved money, bought their freedom, and rose to high positions. The early church was made up mainly of the poor and of slaves.
p121.011: People generally took the class they were born into for granted. The Urantia Book explains that Christianity was never an economic movement meant to change the condition of oppressed classes. It also says that the devotion and love of Jewish families were far better than those of the gentile world.
p121.013: In the minds of the gentiles there was good soil in which good seed could grow. At that time there were four great philosophies: the Epicureans, who sought happiness; the Stoics, who taught high morals but did not know a loving Father God; the Cynics, who preached simplicity and virtue in the fields and the marketplaces; and the Skeptics, who doubted every certainty.
p121.014: These philosophies were noble, but they were mostly for the strong and the wise; they were not a religion that saved even the poor and the weak. Still, the Cynic preachers prepared spiritually hungry people for the gospel preachers who would come later.
p121.016: Most of the older religions were matters of the tribe or the nation, so they did not satisfy the spiritual longing of each individual. In the West in the time of Jesus there were the ceremonies of the old myths, emperor worship, astrology, and the mystery religions. The mystery religions centered on stories of a god who died and came back to life, and they promised salvation after death through secret rituals.
p121.017: The Urantia Book says not to confuse the teachings of Jesus with the mystery religions. The popularity of the mystery religions only shows how thirsty people were for true personal religion. The Christianity that Paul preached gave up magical rituals and taught a new moral life, and it was built not on myth but on the historical fact that Michael had actually come to human beings.
p121.019: In Palestine in the time of Jesus, the common people spoke Aramaic, the priests and rabbis Hebrew, and educated people Greek. As the Hebrew scriptures were translated into Greek, Jewish thought was greatly influenced by Greek philosophy. Philo of Alexandria was a great teacher who wove Greek philosophy and Hebrew theology together, and Paul built on his ideas.
p121.020: The Urantia Book says that some of Paul’s doctrines of original sin and atonement came from Mithraism or were Paul’s own ideas, and have almost nothing in common with the teachings of Jesus. The Jews scattered all over the world all made the temple at Jerusalem the center of their hearts and waited for the Messiah.
p121.022: The Jews built a high wall between themselves and the gentile world and were tightly bound to the letter of the law and to tradition. Because they expected a Messiah who would come out of their own nation’s history, it was hard for them to accept the generous teaching of Jesus that saw all peoples as brothers. In the end they could not break the chains of tradition, and so they failed in their mission to carry the new gospel.
p121.023: So the development of religion passed to the peoples of western Europe. Paul’s Christianity mixed the gospel of Jesus with Greek philosophy, the teachings of the mystery religions, and the strong morals of Judaism. People in those days believed that even rocks and trees had spirits in them and thought of miracles as ordinary, so they could not help being amazed at the new words of the carpenter of Nazareth.
p121.025: The writer says he also made use of the four gospels along with Andrew’s lost record. The Gospel of Mark was written first and most briefly, based on the memories of Peter. The Gospel of Matthew was actually written by Isador, a disciple of Matthew, based on Matthew’s notes, for Jewish believers. The Gospel of Luke was put together by Luke the physician from what he heard from Paul and many eyewitnesses, and the Gospel of John was written by John’s associate Nathan, with John supplying his memories. These records are incomplete, but they were enough to change the course of the world for almost two thousand years.
p121.026: Finally, the writer explains that wherever possible he used the thoughts and expressions people had left behind, and used heavenly information only when those were not enough. He worked, he says, as a collector and editor who gathered the best thoughts of more than two thousand people. This story of how Jesus came at the best possible time reminds us that the will of God is present in our own times and surroundings too.
p122.002: It is hard to explain fully why Michael chose Palestine, and why he chose the family of Joseph and Mary. After looking over many worlds, Michael chose Urantia as the place for his final bestowal, that is, for living as a creature himself. Gabriel personally looked over our world and recommended the Hebrew people, and a commission of twelve studied Jewish families and put forward three couples as candidates. From among them, Gabriel himself chose Joseph and Mary.
p122.004: Joseph was a carpenter, from a family of craftsmen such as builders and stoneworkers going back for generations. The Urantia Book makes clear that Joseph was not a direct descendant of David and Solomon. Mary was an ordinary woman of her time, but many of her ancestors were remarkable women. The Urantia Book explains that Mary was Jewish in culture and belief, but she had the blood of many peoples mixed in her.
p122.005: Michael wanted to be born an ordinary person so that ordinary people could understand and accept him. That is why Gabriel chose as parents people like Joseph and Mary, who were ordinary and yet had good character.
p122.007: The work of Jesus actually began with John the Baptist. John’s parents, Zacharias and Elizabeth, had gone without a child for a long time. Gabriel appeared to Elizabeth and told her that she would soon have a son and that the child would prepare the way for a divine teacher. At first Zacharias doubted it very much, but later he became sure of it through a dream.
p122.008: After meeting Gabriel, Mary too went to visit Elizabeth and stayed three weeks, sharing their experiences with each other, and their faith grew stronger. John was born in March of 7 B.C., and from childhood he grew up with the idea that he would become a spiritual leader.
p122.010: One day around sunset, Gabriel appeared to Mary and told her that she would have a son and should name him Joshua. He said that this son would begin the kingdom of heaven on earth. Mary kept this in her heart for several weeks and then told Joseph. Joseph trusted his wife deeply, but he was so troubled that he could not sleep for many nights.
p122.011: The Urantia Book says that Gabriel’s visit was the only supernatural event in the whole process of Mary conceiving and giving birth to Jesus. Mary’s parents and brothers and sisters always tended to doubt Jesus’ mission.
p122.013: Joseph became sure only after he met a heavenly messenger in a dream. The messenger said that in the child would be life, and “⟦Q 122:4.1⟧his life shall become the light of mankind⟦/Q⟧”. In all these visits nothing was ever said about the house of David or about a deliverer of the Jews. Jesus was not the Messiah the Jews expected but the deliverer of the world, for all peoples.
p122.014: The Urantia Book explains that many Old Testament prophecies were interpreted to fit Jesus after he had gone. For example, the passage “⟦Q 122:4.4⟧a maiden shall bear a son⟦/Q⟧” was changed to read “⟦Q 122:4.4⟧a virgin shall bear a son⟦/Q⟧”, and the family trees made later cannot be trusted as they stand either.
p122.016: Joseph was a gentle man who spoke little and thought deeply, and Mary was always cheerful, frank, and practical. From his father Jesus inherited gentleness and a heart that understands people, and from his mother the gift of teaching and the power of righteous indignation. He also learned from his father a deep knowledge of the Hebrew scriptures, and from his mother a broader view of religion and spiritual freedom.
p122.017: For their time, the two were well educated and were fine teachers. Their love began on the day Joseph was helping with work on Mary’s house and Mary brought him a cup of water. Joseph tended to think of the Messiah as a spiritual teacher, and Mary as a political deliverer.
p122.019: Jesus’ home was near the hill north of Nazareth, at the edge of the village. Thanks to that, as he grew up, Jesus often walked in the fields and climbed to the top of the hill. The house was a one-room stone house with a flat roof, and a low stone table, a loom, a lampstand, and some mats were about all the furnishings. Young Jesus used to feed the grain in while his mother turned the millstone.
p122.021: When the Roman emperor Augustus ordered a census, Joseph had to go to Bethlehem to register. Mary did not really need to go, but she was worried that the baby might be born while she was alone, so she insisted on going along. On August 18, 7 B.C., the two set out with Mary riding on a pack animal.
p122.022: On the way, Joseph talked about the child becoming a spiritual teacher, and Mary about him becoming the deliverer of the Jewish nation. When they reached Bethlehem, the inn and their relatives’ homes were all full, so they stayed in a grain storage room beside a stable cut into the rock.
p122.024: At noon on August 21, 7 B.C., with the help of other travelers, Mary gave birth to a son, and the baby was laid in a nearby manger. Jesus was born in exactly the same way as every other baby. At that time angels sang over the manger, but human ears could not hear them.
p122.025: Three priests from Ur, sent by Zacharias, came to visit and left gifts, but The Urantia Book says there was no star that they followed. That year there was a natural event when Jupiter and Saturn appeared to come together, and from this the legend of the star of Bethlehem arose. Joseph’s family stayed in Bethlehem for a while, thinking they might raise Jesus in the city of David.
p122.027: Following the law of Moses, Joseph and Mary went to the temple in Jerusalem and held the ceremony of presenting Jesus, their firstborn son. In the temple were Simeon, a singer, and Anna, a poetess, who had heard about Jesus from Zacharias and believed in him as the Messiah. Simeon amazed the people by singing a poem Anna had written. It spoke of a light to shine “⟦Q 122:9.21⟧upon those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death⟦/Q⟧”. Joseph felt uneasy seeing people so eager to look on the baby as the Messiah.
p122.029: When King Herod heard about the priests from Ur and the song sung in the temple, he wanted to get rid of the new “⟦Q 122:10.1⟧king of the Jews⟦/Q⟧”. When he could not find the baby, he ordered the boy babies of Bethlehem under two years old to be killed, and sixteen babies lost their lives in one day. One of Herod’s officials who believed in the Messiah sent word to Zacharias, and Joseph’s family had fled to Alexandria in Egypt the night before.
p122.030: They lived there for two years and came back after Herod died. The story of the Creator of the whole universe growing up as the baby of a poor couple, protected in the midst of danger, shows how precious ordinary life and family are.
p123.002: Joseph’s family, who had gone to Alexandria to escape Herod, stayed in a relative’s home, and Joseph soon found work and even became a building supervisor. Mary cherished little Jesus dearly and always wanted to keep him close, but Joseph persuaded her that the child needed to play with children his own age. Mary also came to realize that too much protection could make a child self-centered, and she allowed Jesus to grow up like other children.
p123.003: Their friends in Alexandria gave Jesus a copy of the Greek scriptures and urged the family to stay in Egypt. But in the end the family returned to Palestine. Mary wanted to raise the child in Bethlehem, the city of David, but Joseph spent three weeks persuading her that Judea was dangerous and Galilee was a better place to raise a child. And so the family set out for Nazareth.
p123.005: When they got back to Nazareth, Jesus was about three years and two months old. He was very happy to have a home of his own, but he missed his friends in Alexandria. Joseph and Mary promised each other not to tell anyone that Jesus was the child of promise, and they kept that promise to the end.
p123.006: Jesus became best friends with Jacob, a neighbor boy, and when his little brother James was born, he would watch the baby for hours. Joseph built a workshop near the village spring, beside the place where caravans stopped to rest. There Jesus grew up listening to the stories of travelers from all over the world.
p123.008: In the year he turned five, Jesus reached the age of making his first wholehearted moral decision, and at this time his Thought Adjuster came. The Thought Adjuster is the divine spirit that God the Father sends into the human mind. Like countless other children, Jesus did not know that this divine guest had come.
p123.009: That year his little sister Miriam was born. From age five to ten, Jesus was truly a never-ending question mark, and although Joseph and Mary could not answer every question, they helped him think things through together and find answers. Following the custom of the Galilean Jews, after age five the father took charge of his son’s education. His mother taught him how to tend a garden, and on the roof Jesus drew maps and practiced writing in a sandbox.
p123.010: 3. Events of the Sixth Year (1 B.C.)
p123.011: Around the age of six, Jesus learned Greek from his father, and using the Greek scriptures he had been given as his textbook, he was soon reading easily. Since there were only two such copies of the scriptures in Nazareth, many people came to their home. One day, when Jesus asked the cause of an earthquake, Joseph answered, “⟦Q 123:3.2⟧My son, I really do not know.⟦/Q⟧” It was his first shock at finding out that even parents do not know everything.
p123.012: That year the family of his cousin John came to visit, and Jesus became very interested in the history of Israel and its many feasts. Also, after finishing the prayers he had been taught, Jesus always insisted on having “⟦Q 123:3.6⟧just a little talk with my Father in heaven⟦/Q⟧”, and even when his parents tried to stop him, he would not change this habit.
p123.013: Joseph started doing building work and his income grew a great deal, and Jesus went along with his father to many villages and learned how people lived. When Joseph patiently explained the reasons for the rules, Jesus gladly followed them. In his free time he looked at flowers and plants by day and at the stars by night.
p123.015: In January of his seventh year, the deepest snow in a hundred years fell on Nazareth. In those days the games of Jewish children were mostly about imitating weddings or funerals, and Jesus played with pieces of wood in a corner of the workshop. Jesus managed the charity fund that Mary had saved up by selling doves.
p123.016: One day during a sandstorm, Jesus fell on the stone steps leading to the roof. The Urantia Book explains that this was an unavoidable accident, and that heavenly beings do not usually step into material accidents at will. Jesus’ childhood was not very different from that of an ordinary lively boy. That year his little brother Joseph was born.
p123.018: In the summer when he was seven, Jesus entered the synagogue school and learned Hebrew and the law. There were no textbooks; the teacher would say a sentence, and the students would repeat it together. Jesus soon became skilled in Hebrew and even read the scriptures at the Sabbath services. At his graduation, his teacher said that he seemed to have learned more from Jesus’ questions than he had taught him.
p123.019: The “⟦Q 123:5.11⟧birthday text⟦/Q⟧” that Jesus chose was the words of Isaiah about bringing good news to the meek and liberty to the captives. Nazareth was a crossroads where caravans came and went, so Jesus met people of many nations. The Urantia Book says that Jesus’ real education came from mixing with people, and that because he understood and loved people so deeply, he was a very highly educated person.
p123.020: On Sabbath afternoons he climbed the hill with his father, looked out over Mount Carmel and Mount Hermon, the Jordan valley and the distant sea, and listened to stories of the prophets of old. Jesus talked with the villagers at the spring, learned to milk, make cheese, and weave, and, watching the skill of Nathan the potter, enjoyed playing with clay with his friend Jacob.
p123.022: In his eighth year Jesus was a hardworking student in the top third of his class. One week each month he stayed at the home of his uncle, a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee, or of his mother’s brother, who had a farm. He met a teacher of mathematics and grew interested in numbers, and he learned to play the harp, becoming a skillful player by the age of eleven. He also taught his little brother James the letters, and that year his little brother Simon was born.
p123.023: Nahor, a teacher from Jerusalem, came and urged that Jesus be educated in Jerusalem. When his parents disagreed, Jesus said that he would “⟦Q 123:6.9⟧talk with my Father who is in heaven⟦/Q⟧”, and then said he would stay home. His reason was that parents who loved him could guide him better than strangers could. This picture of young Jesus trusting his parents and asking God shows us what to do when we have an important decision to make.
p124.002: If Jesus had stayed in Alexandria, he might have gone to better schools. But in Nazareth he could work out the problems of life for himself and meet all kinds of people from all over the world. Because of this, Jesus was prepared to understand not only Jews but gentiles as well, and he came to see both the Eastern and the Western views of the Jewish faith in balance.
p124.004: When he was nine, there was a big uproar at school. Jewish law forbade making images or pictures, but Jesus loved drawing and modeling clay, and he was caught drawing his teacher’s face on the classroom floor. When the elders came to Joseph to protest, Jesus boldly spoke his own mind, but he also said he would follow his father’s decision. Joseph decided to keep the law, and from then on, as long as he lived at home, Jesus did not draw pictures. Giving up a hobby he loved was a great trial.
p124.005: That year Jesus climbed Mount Tabor for the first time, and his little sister Martha was born. His father made him a small workbench. Seeing ice for the first time, Jesus thought deeply about the material world as he watched water change into ice, water, and steam. The Urantia Book says that this boy was actually the Creator who made the whole universe. Before he turned ten, Jesus became the leader of a group of seven boys who wanted to build up body, mind, and religion together.
p124.007: At ten, Jesus first began to sense that his life mission was special, and he talked to his parents about it, but they told him nothing. In the eyes of his friends Jesus was a boy no different from them, except that he asked a few more questions.
p124.008: The most unusual thing about Jesus was that even when he was treated unfairly, he would not fight for his own rights. His friend Jacob, a year older, protected him so that no one could treat him roughly. Because Jesus was fair and understood people deeply, he was a leader his friends loved, and he also enjoyed talking with grown-ups about many subjects. That year, fishing with his uncle, he was becoming a skillful fisherman.
p124.010: When he was eleven, his little brother Jude was born, and because his mother became very ill, Jesus took on the responsibilities of the eldest son early. From then on Jesus could never go back to the innocence of childhood. Joseph and Mary were tempted to treat Jesus as special, but they wisely held back, and Jesus also refused special treatment.
p124.011: When Jesus went with his father to the Greek city of Scythopolis, he was deeply impressed by the athletic games and said it would be good if the young men of Nazareth could have sports like that too. Joseph, who disliked gentile games, became angry with Jesus that night for the first and only time. Jesus answered, “⟦Q 124:3.8⟧Very well, my father, it shall be so.⟦/Q⟧” He never brought up the subject again, but later, when he was with his apostles, he valued wholesome recreation. From around this time, Jesus thought deeply about how to fulfill both his duty to his family and his mission to the world.
p124.013: At twelve, Jesus began working regularly in the home workshop, and he managed his own earnings. There were many times he struggled because he was not sure what his mission was. Joseph and Mary sensed that there was something special in their son, but they never knew that he was the Creator of the universe. Jesus leaned more and more toward his father’s spiritual ideas, and his mother was disappointed by this.
p124.014: Jesus asked whether the custom of kissing the parchment on the doorpost was not idolatry, just like making pictures, and Joseph took the parchment down. During this time Jesus was torn between the command to be loyal to truth and righteousness and the command to honor his parents. But he did not run away from the difficulty; day by day he brought the two into harmony and learned a family unity founded on loyalty, fairness, and love.
p124.016: When he turned thirteen, Jesus’ voice began to change. His youngest brother Amos was born, and around February Jesus became certain that he had a mission to enlighten people and reveal God. In March he graduated from the synagogue school and became a “⟦Q 124:5.4⟧son of the commandment⟦/Q⟧”, a responsible citizen of Israel.
p124.017: The elders wanted to send Jesus to a famous school in Jerusalem, but Jesus felt that he would not go. He did not yet know that, with his father’s coming death, he would soon be responsible for a large family. Later Jesus became a wise and patient eldest brother and teacher to that family.
p124.019: In the spring of the year he graduated, Jesus went to Jerusalem with his parents to keep the Passover for the first time. Along the way through the Jordan valley, avoiding Samaria, his parents told him the stories of ancient Israel connected with each place. In Bethany they met the family of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, and they became lifelong friends. When he first looked out on Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, Jesus felt the greatest human thrill of his life.
p124.020: Jesus was deeply moved by the temple ceremonies, but he also asked why God the Father needed so many innocent animals to be killed. On the night before the Passover Sabbath, Jesus’ heart was filled with love and pity for the spiritually blind crowds. Then a heavenly messenger appeared and said, “⟦Q 124:6.15⟧It is time that you began to be about your Father's business.⟦/Q⟧”
p124.021: So ended the boyhood days in Nazareth, and the story of the teenage Jesus, who more and more comes to realize who he is, begins. When we remember that Jesus, like us, grew up struggling between his parents’ hopes, his own dreams, and his responsibility to his family, our own struggles feel a little more precious.
p125.002: Nothing in the life of Jesus was more thrilling than this first visit to Jerusalem. In particular, the few days in the week after the Passover when he took part on his own in the temple discussions were the first time, and for a long time the last, that he enjoyed freedom from all responsibility. Jesus had said he would not go unless his mother went too, so more women than usual came along on this pilgrimage.
p125.003: Seen from outside, the temple was more than he had expected, but once he stepped inside, his disappointment began. When his mother could not join him at the consecration ceremony and had to go off separately to the women’s section, Jesus was deeply indignant at that unfairness. When his parents explained the meaning of the temple ceremonies in terms of the wrath of God, Jesus said that the Father in heaven could not love his children less than an earthly father does. After that, his parents did not try to change their son’s ideas about the love of God.
p125.005: As he looked around the temple courts, Jesus was shocked by the irreverent attitude of the people there. In the court of the gentiles, money-changers and merchants selling animals for sacrifice were mixed together, making a noisy racket, and the place was full of sights that did not belong in a holy place. When he saw animals being slaughtered and blood flowing in the court of the priests, the boy who loved nature could not bear it and begged his father to take him away.
p125.006: Joseph took his son to the Beautiful Gate to cheer him up and explained the feasts that were kept three times a year. Jesus admired the beautiful rituals of the temple, but in the faces of the many people worshiping without thought, he saw spiritual ugliness.
p125.008: The family ate the Passover meal at Simon’s house in Bethany. Jesus, now newly a son of the law, told the story of the origin of the Passover, but his thoughts about what he had recently seen and heard were quietly mixed in, which upset his parents. Jesus was convinced that the Father in heaven did not take pleasure in sacrifices, and he resolved that someday he would establish a Passover without blood. That night neither Jesus nor his parents slept much.
p125.009: During Passover week Jesus went around to the temple discussion groups, talking with more than one hundred fifty young people his age from all over the world and learning how people lived. Lazarus, Martha, and Mary came to love Jesus like their own brother. His parents did not know what to do as they watched their son sit lost in deep thought with his head buried in his hands.
p125.011: When the Passover was over and the Nazareth group set out, Jesus was so absorbed in a temple discussion about angels that he forgot the time to leave. In those days men and women traveled in separate groups, and Mary thought her son was with the men, while Joseph thought he was with the women. Only when they reached Jericho did they find that Jesus was missing, and they spent a sleepless night. The two blamed each other for not checking whether their son was in the group before leaving Jerusalem.
p125.012: 4. First and Second Days in the Temple
p125.013: Jesus spent the night in Bethany and the next morning set out for the temple again. On the Mount of Olives, he wept as he looked out on a people bound by tradition and living under the watch of Roman soldiers. That day Jesus took an active part in the discussions, and he even asked whether it was just to put to death a gentile who had unknowingly entered the sacred area of the temple. One teacher raised the question of his age and mocked him for coming from Nazareth, but the leader of the discussion ruled that Jesus could go on taking part. Meanwhile Joseph and Mary wandered all over Jerusalem all day long. The teachers were sometimes caught off guard by Jesus’ sharp questions, but seeing his honest desire to learn and his fair attitude, most of them treated him politely.
p125.014: 5. The Third Day in the Temple
p125.015: On the third day many people gathered to see the Galilean boy who was confounding the experts in the law. Jesus asked what was behind the veil of the Holy of Holies, why mothers had to be kept apart, why so many animals had to be killed if God is a loving Father, whether it was right to do business in the temple, and whether the Messiah was a worldly king or a spiritual light.
p125.016: Jesus taught more by asking questions than by giving answers, and he won people’s hearts with words that blended wisdom and humor. He never tried to win arguments to show off; he was always fair, and he cared only about making the truth known. That night Jesus thought until late about how to set the people free from the bondage of tradition, but no clear answer had come yet.
p125.017: 6. The Fourth Day in the Temple
p125.018: On the fourth day, the leader of the discussion seated Jesus beside him and asked him to share his thoughts about prayer and worship. Just then Joseph and Mary, passing through the temple, recognized their son’s voice. Mary scolded her son in front of everyone, saying that they had been searching anxiously for three days, and so the great opportunity to share the truth came to an end. After a moment’s thought Jesus answered, “⟦Q 125:6.7⟧Would you not expect to find me in my Father's house⟦/Q⟧”?
p125.019: Then, comforting his parents by saying that no one had done anything but what he thought best, he set out for home with them. On the Mount of Olives, Jesus grieved over Jerusalem, enslaved by tradition, and cried out that someday he would come back and cleanse the temple. When he got home, he said, “⟦Q 125:6.11⟧I will await my hour.⟦/Q⟧” and promised that while doing the will of his Father in heaven, he would also obey his father on earth.
p125.020: Mary took this event as a sign that her son would become the political deliverer of Israel. But even when he could not agree, Jesus did his best to fit in with his family. The way Jesus kept his convictions while still respecting his family shows us what to do when we see things differently from our parents.
